title: Lion City: After Hours
observed_goal: On the page/menu text, the stated goal is one night with six contracts; its execution was not observed in the frames; the available evidence is inconclusive.
observed_controls: In the page text and frames, Enter for Select and Esc for Back are visible.

No dedicated driving, movement, vehicle-selection, or in-game interaction controls were observed as active; the available evidence is inconclusive; the metadata also records controls_attempted as empty.
observed_core_loop: No active gameplay loop, driving, contract, pursuit, or delivery was observed in the frames; the available evidence is inconclusive.
progress_feedback: The main menu shows a counter of 0/6 contracts and $250 banked; a change to it was not observed in the frames; the available evidence is inconclusive.
decisions_risk_reward: No executable decisions or risk/reward were observed; the available evidence is inconclusive. The official card text claims high-risk drift, cash, and increasing police heat, but this claim was not confirmed through gameplay.
rewards: The initial amount of $250 banked is visible in the menu; the source and mechanism for earning rewards were not observed in gameplay; the available evidence is inconclusive. The official claim about cash and score has not yet been playtested.
penalties_failure: No penalty, failure, arrest, or loss of progress was observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
outcomes_replay: No win, loss, contract outcome, end of loop, or replay evidence was observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
onboarding: The main menu is visible with the options HIT THE STREETS, RECORDS, CONTROLS, and SETTINGS and language selection EN/中文; successful entry into the game or interactive tutorial was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
visual_audio_accessibility: The frames show a 3D nighttime menu with neon contrast and the EN/中文 language option. Audio cannot be evaluated from the frames; according to the trace, AudioContext was not allowed to start automatically. Text size, legibility, and full accessibility were not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
technical_clues: The page was recorded with HTTP 200 and page_status=loaded and has multiple canvases with recorded dimensions; this is only a technical clue and does not establish that the game is active.

The console recorded a WebGL software fallback warning and 404, 403, 400 errors, as well as failure to receive remote config; their effect on the game was not observed; the available evidence is inconclusive.
AudioContext was not allowed to start because there was no user gesture; this is a technical clue and by itself does not establish that the game has no sound.
transferable_principles: Reflect a multi-stage goal with a simple, readable counter on the same initial screen.
Design and test risk and reward only after observing the real loop and with understandable feedback.
Display the primary inputs and the active state of the game explicitly and accessibly before relying on a change of frame.
In the event of a loading or media-start error, provide a fallback state and a clear message, and evaluate it separately from the game logic.
candle_climber_relevance: For Candle Climber, score/rank should reflect only skill and performance, not purchases or wallet and not an economic advantage.
Any risk/reward pattern is transferable from this evidence only as a hypothesis requiring testing; its implementation should be examined with clear feedback and without guessing about the controls.
I do not recommend free brake, horizontal direction change, or a branching path requiring a new control; if examined, it should be only a separate hypothesis requiring testing.
do_not_copy: Do not reproduce the official claim about an open world, vehicle classes, contracts, drift, or police heat as a confirmed capability.
Do not reproduce or propose this game’s name, characters, art, level, text, sound, brand, or assets.
Do not use a change between two frames to draw conclusions about input acceptance, progress, or the game loop.
Do not treat the absence of an element in the initial frame as its absence from the entire game.

evidence.claim: The load, after_start, after_key_burst, and after_combined_input frames all show the main menu with HIT THE STREETS, RECORDS, CONTROLS, SETTINGS, and 0/6 contracts · $250 banked; active gameplay or an execution result is not visible.
The page text in the after_start, after_key_burst, after_combined_input, and late stages records the same main menu and the Enter/Select and Esc/Back instructions.

The official card claims that the game includes a compact open city, 9 vehicle classes, drift for cash, increasing police heat, and 6 courier contracts; this claim was not confirmed through playtesting.
The metadata says controls_attempted is empty, start_action=none, and interaction_visual_change_signal=null; a possible visual change is not proof of input acceptance.
The trace includes AudioContext blocked, HTTP 404/403/400 errors, failure of remote config, and a WebGL software fallback.

limitations: Only the input files for this game were examined, and no web browsing was performed. capture_status=partial; the load, after_start, and late screenshots are from fallback-1, while the two middle frames are from current. Several screenshots timed out, the generic keyboard sequence was omitted because focus was on a text/select input, and there is no frame showing active gameplay, a complete loop, an outcome, or accepted input. The metadata records no visual change, but any frame change, if present, could be due to animation or elapsed time.
